title: Cardinal Rental Reimbursement Partner Invoice: Covered Days and Agency Payment Amount
content:
## 1. The rental invoiced

The invoice is paid for the claim's most recently closed rental. That rental's start date, the daily rate recorded on its authorization, the end date of its closing and its authorized days (the authorization plus every extension of it) are read from the rental ledger of the Cardinal Rental Reimbursement option.

## 2. Covered days

The covered days of a partner invoice are the closed span of the rental. The span is counted from its start date through the end date of its closing, with both days included. The covered days are never more than the rental's authorized days.

## 3. Agency payment

The agency payment is the covered days multiplied by the lower of two figures: the rate recorded on the authorization, and the option's daily limit. The payment is never above what the per-loss maximum still allows. That is the option's per-loss maximum less the agency payments and reimbursements already on the claim, net of agency credits. The payment is never below zero, and it is rounded to the cent.

## Worked computation (hypothetical figures, Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 50/1500)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Start date and closing end date | June 1 to June 12 |
| Closed span (both days included) | 12 days |
| Authorized days (7 on the authorization plus 5 on one extension) | 12 days |
| Covered days (span, no more than the authorized days) | 12 |
| Rate recorded on the authorization; daily limit | $54.99; $50.00 |
| Lower of the two | $50.00 |
| Covered days multiplied by $50.00 | $600.00 |
| Per-loss maximum less $1000.00 already paid on the claim, no agency credits | $500.00 |
| Agency payment | $500.00 |

## A shorter authorization (hypothetical)

A rental runs from March 3 through March 11. That is a closed span of 9 days, on an authorization of 7 days with no extension. The covered days are 7. At a recorded rate of $38.40 on Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 40/1200, the lower figure is $38.40. The payment is 7 multiplied by $38.40, which is $268.80, provided the per-loss maximum still allows that much.
